Life from age 4 to 16

I usually want somebody to show me the first part, and then I can work from there. Helping at home has made me curious about nursing, but I have not seen enough of the work to know what it is really like.

  • family: Lives with his father, aunt, and grandmother.
  • finances: Tight budget; essentials are stable but optional transport is difficult.
  • geography: Small community outside Brownsville, Texas.
  • cultureLanguages: Spanish and English at home.
  • school: Public high school with biology but no accessible laboratory club.
  • accessOpportunities: Library and classroom projects; no clinic observation or paid work yet.
  • Age 4–5

    In 2014, Sam enjoyed quiet picture-book afternoons with his aunt and making toy roads across the floor. He preferred adults to show him a new game before asking him to explain how he would play.

  • Age 6–7

    At six, he learned classroom routines slowly at first and then followed them reliably. During 2017, he liked helping put shared materials away, particularly when a teacher explained where unfamiliar objects belonged without making the question embarrassing.

  • Age 8–9

    In 2018, Sam began reminding his grandmother about ordinary household plans, such as a scheduled call or a prepared meal. Adults remained responsible for medical decisions, and Sam also spent plenty of afternoons playing outside with cousins.

  • Age 10–11

    During 2020, he helped household members remember the order of online school sessions. He often asked his aunt to check unfamiliar instructions, even when he later completed the task without further help once the first step was clear.

  • Age 12–13

    At twelve, Sam enjoyed a biology project and noticed small changes in how a relative felt during everyday routines. In 2023, he became curious about how trained staff support people over time rather than deciding diagnoses alone.

  • Age 14–15

    Across 2024 and 2025, Sam had no clinic access, laboratory club, or paid job. School science and household reminders remained his actual experience, while conversations with a teacher introduced nursing observation as something he could investigate.

  • Age 16

    At sixteen in 2026, Sam is exploring Texas nursing programs and asking how a first observation might be arranged. He is open to structured learning without assuming graduate study, and his cautious language reflects unfamiliarity rather than a conclusion about what he could learn.

Life now

  • enjoys: Biology · Helping with ordinary routines · Quiet family time
  • avoids: Pretending to know an unfamiliar task · Being rushed past questions
  • activities: Biology project · Household reminders
  • demonstratedSkills: Follows familiar routines · Notices everyday changes · Asks for clarification
  • unfamiliarActivities: Clinical care · Paid work · Laboratory clubs · Nursing observation
  • motivations: Useful support · Learning with guidance
  • ambitions: Explore an introductory observation and nursing study · He imagines a steady life near supportive people with enough independence to manage his own routines.
  • struggles: Low confidence with unfamiliar activities · Limited opportunities to try them
  • supports: Father · Aunt · Science teacher
  • practicalConstraints: Transport · Program fees · Few local introductions

Still uncertain: What changes after a supportive first introduction? · Which aspects of care would appeal beyond familiar family routines?

Career: Registered Nurses

Preparation: Texas RN license or valid compact privilege.

  • Graduate from an approved nursing program.
  • Pass NCLEX-RN and the Texas nursing law exam.
  • Complete the Board application and fingerprinting.

Training budget before aid: $111,516 · 3.0 study years in this reference

Still needs funding: $111,516 · loan payments $0/month · included in lifestyle: no

Annual pay before tax: $74,370 · TWC entry-wage proxy · entry

Chosen-life income range: $55,000–$65,000

Budget result: This pay covers your lifestyle. Your costs and savings fit, with money left over.

Financial assumptions: Supported wishes: steadiness, supportive people and independent routines. Each price-level choice is a modest single-adult reference, including transit and savings, not an ambition ceiling inferred from current transport or fees.
